This vignette covers the two things people ask for first: how to reproduce the
visualizations published in the dbVisuals Application Note, and how to start each
of the package's entry points.

## Install

The rendering packages and database dependencies come from CRAN.

```{r}
install.packages(c("DBI", "duckdb", "rDeckgl", "rMosaic"))

# or let the package do it
dbVisuals::install_dbvisuals_deps()
```

`dbVisuals` itself is not on CRAN yet:

```{r}
remotes::install_github("dbverse-org/dbVisuals2@paper-repro", subdir = "r-package")
```

## Entry point 1 — the SQLRooms browser workspace

`launchBrowser()` starts a local server plus the packaged front end and opens a
browser. Point it at a DuckDB file, or omit `db_path` for an empty in-memory
database you can populate from the UI.

```{r}
library(dbVisuals)

# empty in-memory database
launchBrowser()

# an existing DuckDB / GiottoDB file
launchBrowser(db_path = "WTA_Preview_FFPE_Breast_Cancer_xenium.duckdb")

stop_sqlrooms()
```

The server always runs in a background process, so the R session stays usable
either way; `daemon` is kept only for backwards compatibility. Ports default to
3001 (server) and 5173 (front end). Only one workspace runs at a time — a second
`launchBrowser()` replaces the first even on different ports — so use two R
sessions if you need two databases side by side.

To push data from R into the running workspace, open your own connection to the
same file you launched. `con` below is that connection; without it
`dplyr::tbl()` has nothing to read and fails with "Invalid connection".

```{r}
db <- file.path(tempdir(), "workspace.duckdb")
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), db)
DBI::dbWriteTable(con, "gdb_cell_metadata",
                  data.frame(x = rnorm(200), y = rnorm(200)))

launchBrowser(db_path = db, browser = FALSE)

# a data frame -> a table in the project database
sqlrooms_export_table("cars", mtcars)

# a lazy dbplyr pipeline -> a view, without pulling it into R
dplyr::tbl(con, "gdb_cell_metadata") |>
  dplyr::filter(x > 0) |>
  sqlrooms_register("cells_pos", x = _)

stop_sqlrooms()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```

## Entry point 2 — R-side linked views with `mosaic_gl()`

`mosaic_gl()` is an htmlwidget: Mosaic views and GPU deck.gl layers in one
browser scope, over a single DuckDB-WASM coordinator and a single shared
selection, so brushing any panel filters all of them. No server, no browser
workspace — it renders in the RStudio viewer, a knitted document, or Shiny.

A self-contained example that needs no database:

```{r}
library(dbVisuals)

pts <- data.frame(x = rnorm(5000), y = rnorm(5000))

spec <- mgl_spec(
  data   = list(pts = mgl_data(type = "table", df = pts)),
  params = list(sel = list(select = "crossfilter")),
  vconcat = list(
    list(
      plot = list(
        list(mark = "dot", data = list(from = "pts", filterBy = "$sel"),
             x = "x", y = "y"),
        list(select = "intervalX", as = "$sel")
      ),
      width = 800, height = 160
    ),
    mgl_deckgl(
      id        = "map",
      filter_by = "$sel",
      width     = 800, height = 460,
      layers = list(list(
        `@@type`         = "ScatterplotLayer",
        id               = "pts",
        data             = "pts",
        getPosition      = "@@=[x, y]",
        getFillColor     = c(100L, 180L, 255L, 220L),
        getRadius        = 3,
        radiusUnits      = "pixels",
        coordinateSystem = "@@#COORDINATE_SYSTEM.CARTESIAN",
        positionFormat   = "XY"
      ))
    )
  )
)

mosaic_gl(spec)
```

Data reaches the browser as Arrow IPC, not JSON. `mgl_data(type = "table")`
serializes a data frame; `mgl_data(type = "duckdb", query = ...)` keeps the data
in the database and ships only the query result, which is what you want for
anything large:

```{r}
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), "my.duckdb", read_only = TRUE)

spec <- mgl_spec(
  data = list(
    cells = mgl_data(
      type  = "duckdb",
      query = "SELECT x, y, leiden_clus FROM gdb_cell_metadata"
    ),
    polys = mgl_data(
      type   = "duckdb",
      # Include the key column: the WKB polygon encoder needs both a key
      # (cell_ID / poly_ID / id) and a geometry column, otherwise it falls
      # back to plain Arrow and the polygon layer is dropped at render time.
      query  = "SELECT cell_ID, ST_AsWKB(geom) AS geometry FROM gdb_cell_polygons",
      format = "geoarrow"
    )
  ),
  vconcat = list(
    mgl_deckgl(
      id = "insitu", width = 800, height = 560,
      layers = list(
        list(
          `@@type`         = "GeoArrowPolygonLayer",
          id               = "polys",
          data             = "polys",
          geometryColumn   = "geometry",
          getFillColor     = c(157L, 78L, 221L, 90L),
          stroked          = FALSE,
          coordinateSystem = "@@#COORDINATE_SYSTEM.CARTESIAN",
          positionFormat   = "XY"
        ),
        list(
          `@@type`         = "ScatterplotLayer",
          id               = "cells",
          data             = "cells",
          getPosition      = "@@=[x, y]",
          getFillColor     = c(30L, 41L, 59L, 200L),
          getRadius        = 2,
          radiusUnits      = "pixels",
          coordinateSystem = "@@#COORDINATE_SYSTEM.CARTESIAN",
          positionFormat   = "XY"
        )
      )
    )
  )
)

mosaic_gl(spec, con = con)
```

Passing `con` also lets the widget issue follow-up queries against your R-side
DuckDB while you interact, instead of materializing everything up front. Any
spatial / nanoarrow / geoarrow extensions already loaded on that connection are
reused.

In Shiny use the pair `mosaic_glOutput()` / `renderMosaic_gl()`.

## Entry point 3 — export a spec back out

Specs built in the browser workspace can be pulled back into R as an htmlwidget
for `rMosaic` or `rDeckgl`:

```{r}
dbvisuals_export_htmlwidget(
  spec,
  "panel.html",
  engine = "rMosaic",
  data   = list(pts = pts)
)
```

## Reproducing the published figures

The published in-situ panels need a GiottoDB DuckDB database holding cell
polygons, cell centroids and transcript coordinates — the Application Note uses
the 10x Genomics Atera In Situ Gene Expression, FFPE Human Breast Cancer preview
dataset on the Xenium platform.

The spec patterns are documented in `vignette("visualization-examples",
package = "dbVisuals")`. The two source routes below are tracked on the
`paper-repro` branch under `r-package/examples/`. They are repository examples,
not installed R help examples; the large public input datasets are not bundled.
Use the same branch for the installed package and cloned examples. These are
R-package viewer demonstrations, not measurements of the Canvas/WASM application.

| Script | Renders |
| --- | --- |
| `03_dimred_concat.R` | UMAP / PCA dimension pairs linked to a `leiden_clus` bar |
| `06_in_situ_zoom_overlay_transcripts_interactive.R` | **the published panel** — interactive ROI selection |

`03_dimred_concat.R` needs the separately installed `Giotto` and `GiottoData`
packages and downloads the mini Visium object. Install these using the Giotto
Suite installation instructions before sourcing it. It needs no local database.

These scripts are not installed with the package, so run them from a clone of the
repository with `r-package/` as the working directory:

```bash
git clone --branch paper-repro https://github.com/dbverse-org/dbVisuals2.git
```

```r
setwd("path/to/dbVisuals2/r-package")
source("examples/03_dimred_concat.R")
```

For the in-situ scripts, point the environment at your data and run them from an
interactive session:

```r
setwd("path/to/dbVisuals2/r-package")
Sys.setenv(DBLENS_DEMO_DB = "/path/to/WTA_Preview_FFPE_Breast_Cancer_xenium.duckdb")
Sys.setenv(DBLENS_TRANSCRIPT_FILE = "/path/to/transcripts.parquet")
source("examples/06_in_situ_zoom_overlay_transcripts_interactive.R")
```

Neither variable is required to be set if the files sit in the working directory
under their default names. Optional overrides: `DBLENS_TRANSCRIPT_TABLE` to read
transcripts from a table inside the database instead of a file, and
`DBLENS_ROI_CELL_ID` to centre the region of interest on a specific cell.

Script 06 starts a Shiny app where dragging the `select`
control re-queries just the transcripts inside the chosen region, and `detail`
picks the nested sub-region. Run it from an interactive R session — under
`Rscript` it prints the widget instead of launching Shiny. The published panel is
a full-window capture of the resulting three-view layout.
Missing expression or cell-type annotations are displayed as unavailable, not
replaced with simulated measurements. The panel demonstrates spatial navigation,
not a new biological clustering result.

## Rebuilding the widget bundle

The pre-built browser bundle ships in `inst/htmlwidgets/`, so none of the above
needs `npm`. To rebuild it from source:

```bash
cd inst/viewer-src
npm ci
npm run build
```

## See also

`vignette("visualization-examples", package = "dbVisuals")` builds the same
linked-view patterns from self-contained data, with no database required.

Versions of deck.gl, Mosaic, GeoArrow and Arrow are held to one contract across
this package and the front end; see `COMPATIBILITY.md` and `versions.json` at the
repository root. From that root, run
`npm --prefix frontend/sqlrooms-ai run test:versions` to check the contract.
